subject.title: bug: Duplicate messages sent to Slack

question: Should a maintainer/operator inspect the named Slack session logs now, or wait for reporter-provided Slack message IDs and version details before this issue gets a code path?
rationale: The source shows adjacent protections, but only operational evidence from the named session can determine whether this is already fixed, a duplicate of the block-streaming class, or a separate Slack delivery bug.

options.title: Inspect the named session
options.body: Use gateway delivery logs plus Slack message timestamps/IDs to map the duplicate to a concrete delivery path before deciding close or fix.

options.title: Wait for reporter details
options.body: Keep the issue open but ask for OpenClaw version, Slack message IDs/timestamps, and the triggering message so maintainers are not guessing.

options.title: Close only after match
options.body: Close as implemented only if the logs match a shipped guard such as the block-streaming final suppression or Slack preview fallback readback.

recommendation.title: Inspect the named session
recommendation.body: Use gateway delivery logs plus Slack message timestamps/IDs to map the duplicate to a concrete delivery path before deciding close or fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack dispatch/default work makes steipete the best available routing candidate from the inspected history, though the exact root cause is still unproven.
